reviewer: number_discussion_audit subagent; model-assisted manual review, not an independent human panel
information_access: Observed19 hypothesis known from task; no numerical simulation outcomes accessed.
scope: All47 eligible-prime literal occurrences in38 verse contexts inspected and exactly reconciled with the independently written parser; additional nonprime number-discussion candidates were reviewed across the full lexical scan. Other-nonprime examples are an audit list, not a claim that every conceivable semantic salience classification has been exhausted.

tiers.core_number_discussion: Explicit addition/subtraction/completion, debate/correction/knowledge of a number, count relation with a generalization, enumeration giving a count rationale, or explicit explanation of a stated count function. Status as a quoted/rejected claim does not erase literal mention.
tiers.relational_quantity: Broader numerical correspondence, per-unit multiplication, quantity comparison, alternative legal quantities, symbolic count mapping, open bounds or measurement comparison; some edges involve interpretation.
tiers.symbolic_epistemic_context: A number occurs in a sign, dream, epistemic challenge, oath or special gift; no explicit metacomment on that number itself.
tiers.literal_only: A count is stated without the stronger relationships above.

recommendation: Primary metanumeric branch uses uniform weights across DISTINCT eligible prime values{3,5,7,19}. Borderline annotation changes above do not alter that set. Do not frequency-weight these manual tiers without a separate registered sensitivity analysis. Broad symbolic branch includes11 and thus equals the full literal prime set.
strict_ordinary_cardinal_counts_note: Counts for3 include two distributive forms at4:3 and35:1; excluding these gives17 for3 and leaves all distinct-value candidate sets unchanged.
